project.name: inventory-prd
project.prd:
# Inventory report CLI

Build a small Python 3 standard-library project from this empty Git repository.

The package must expose `parse_rows(lines)`, `summarize(records)`, and
`render_report(records)` from `inventory.py`. Input rows are CSV with columns
`name,quantity,unit_price`; the first row is a header. Reject malformed rows,
negative quantities, and negative prices with a clear `ValueError`. Use decimal
arithmetic for money, not binary floating-point arithmetic.

`summarize` returns total quantity and total inventory value. `render_report`
lists items in case-insensitive alphabetical order with quantities, prices,
line values, and a final total formatted to two decimal places. Equal names
must retain input order.

Provide `python3 -m inventory INPUT.csv` as a CLI that prints the report to
stdout and exits nonzero with a readable error on invalid input. Add
standard-library `unittest` tests covering parsing, invalid input, arithmetic,
ordering, and the CLI. Include a README with run/test commands and a Python
cache `.gitignore`. Do not use third-party packages, network access, a UI,
deployment, or publication.

Acceptance must run behavioral assertions, including a CLI subprocess check
and a decimal arithmetic edge case (`0.10 + 0.20 == 0.30`).

plan.summary: Build a standard-library inventory module and CLI, add behavioral unittest coverage, and document usage. The repository is empty, Python 3.10.16 is available, and there are no existing build or test checks.
assumptions: parse_rows returns a list of dictionaries with name as str, quantity as int, and unit_price as Decimal.
summarize returns (total_quantity, total_value), with total_value as Decimal.
Require the header name,quantity,unit_price and exactly three fields per data row; reject empty names, noninteger quantities, and nonfinite prices.
Render one item per line followed by a total line, using stable case-insensitive sorting and two decimal places for monetary amounts.
The supervisor owns commits and delivery; implementation stays within this worktree.

requirements.description: inventory.py exposes parse_rows, summarize, and render_report using only Python standard-library dependencies.
Parse CSV headers and rows, including quoted names; reject malformed input, negative quantities, and negative prices with clear ValueError messages.
Calculate total quantity and inventory value with Decimal arithmetic, including exact 0.10 + 0.20 == 0.30 behavior.
Render quantities, prices, line values, and a final total; monetary amounts have two decimal places, names sort case-insensitively, and equal names retain input order.
python3 -m inventory INPUT.csv prints the report to stdout and returns a nonzero status with a readable error for invalid input.
Provide standard-library unittest coverage, README run/test commands, and Python cache ignore rules without third-party packages or network usage.

tasks.title: Implement inventory functions and CLI
tasks.instructions: Create inventory.py with the three public functions and an argparse-based module entry point. Use csv and Decimal throughout, validate headers, field counts, names, integer quantities, and finite nonnegative prices, and include row context in errors. Render stable case-insensitive ordering and two-decimal monetary fields. Handle invalid input and file errors with readable stderr and nonzero exit status. Document the selected record shape and summary return type.

tasks.title: Add behavioral acceptance tests
tasks.instructions: Create discoverable unittest tests for valid and quoted CSV, header-only input, malformed headers and field counts, empty names, invalid integers, negative values, and nonfinite prices. Assert error messages are meaningful. Assert Decimal result types and exact decimal edge-case arithmetic. Assert report fields, two-decimal formatting, case-insensitive ordering, and stable duplicate ordering. Use tempfile and subprocess with sys.executable to test CLI success, invalid CSV, and missing files, checking stdout, stderr, and exit codes.

tasks.instructions: Add README.md with CSV examples, public API shapes, validation rules, report format, python3 -m inventory INPUT.csv usage, and python3 -m unittest discover -v. Add .gitignore rules for __pycache__/ and *.py[cod]. Run all acceptance commands, fixing any failures without removing or weakening tests.

import pathlib, subprocess, sys, tempfile

    assert result.returncode != 0
    assert result.stderr.strip(), 'Expected readable error'
    assert not result.stdout, result.stdout
